kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the section's table.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the 13-row tissue-distribution table; the attack structure is a KYP design.

kypExtensions.summary: The two-anchor reading of any adrenergic stem (ANCHOR 1 — NAME THE TISSUE: the stem's organ names the row — heart, bronchioles, pancreas, vessels...; ANCHOR 2 — READ THE RECEPTOR COLUMN, THEN THE EFFECT CELL: the table's own cell supplies the direction). The GRID VIEW itself (tissues down x receptors across — the cross-tabulation of the book's own 13 rows into a 12-tissue x 5-receptor matrix) is KYP's pivot: every cell is the book's own printed element; the matrix view is KYP's. THE EMPTY-CELL CAVEAT (KYP, flagged on the visual and in the note): the table prints positives only — a blank cell means 'no row in the book's table pairs this receptor with this tissue', NOT 'the receptor is absent from the tissue' (real vessels carry alpha2, real airways carry alpha1 — none of that is printed here; do not read absence into silence).
kypExtensions.rationale: The book prints a 13-row list grouped by receptor; the cross-tabulated grid, the reading order (tissue → receptor → effect), and the empty-cell caveat are KYP's design — every filled cell is the book's own.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + blocks[2] the grid pivot + the visual's grid panel

kypExtensions.summary: The three KYP compressions of the table's own cells: (1) THE PANCREAS SEESAW — the table's two pancreas rows (α2 'Inhibition of insulin secretion' vs β2 'Stimulation of insulin secretion'), the only organ with two rows under two receptors — same organ, opposite signs; (2) THE TONE SEESAW — the α1 'Vascular smooth muscle / Vasoconstriction' row vs the β2 'Arterial smooth muscle / Vasodilation' row, two DIFFERENT printed labels carrying the two arms of vascular tone; (3) THE α2 TRIPLE BRAKE — all three printed α2 rows are inhibitions (insulin, neurotransmitter release, salivary secretion): in this table α2 is the brake-pedal receptor, the contraction receptor being α1. The Heart-vs-Cardiac-muscle doubling note (the table prints '↑ heart rate, contractility' under BOTH β1 'Heart' and β2 'Cardiac muscle') is likewise a KYP reading of two printed rows the book never comments on.
kypExtensions.rationale: The frames are built entirely from the table's own printed cells (the two pancreas rows, the vascular/arterial labels, the three inhibition rows, the doubled heart-rate row); the seesaw/brake naming and the doubling note are KYP's synthesis.
kypExtensions.location: blocks[1] captions + usmle.traps + the visual's seesaw cards

kypExtensions.summary: The clinical/drug anchor layer (NONE of it printed on this page, flagged wherever it appears): albuterol/epinephrine on β2 (bronchodilation, vasodilation), dobutamine on β1 (heart + renin), phenylephrine on α1 (vasoconstriction), clonidine on α2 presynaptic terminals (the autoreceptor story the table's 'Inhibition of neurotransmitter release' row implies), mirabegron on β3 (the adipose row here; its bladder story lives on the SAME page's upper portion, PH14 — the same-page cross-link), the epinephrine-anaphylaxis composite (α1 + β2 together), and the juxtaglomerular-apparatus anchor for the Kidney/renin row. The four-code memory layer: '1 HEART, 2 LUNGS, 3 FAT' is the CLASSIC counting code — the book itself prints '(one heart)' and '(two lungs)' in the β1/β2 rows of the G-protein table on the FACING page (book 237, the separate pending topic; carried as the classic code, attributed); the other three codes (α2 IS THE BRAKE PEDAL; THE PANCREAS SEESAW; TWO SMOOTH MUSCLES, TWO SIGNS) are KYP-original compressions of this page's own rows.
kypExtensions.rationale: The drug and clinical anchors extend past the page (the table prints no drug names); the classic counting code is attributed to its facing-page source; the remaining three codes are KYP-original designs built on the section's own rows.
kypExtensions.location: mnemonics + usmle + the visual's code strip

notes: Census (pdfimages + text layer): the Tissue distribution of adrenergic receptors section occupies the LOWER portion of pdf 258 (book 236), directly below the COMPLETED PH14 Micturition control section (same-page boundary pinned). The section's ENTIRE printed content is ONE 13-row table (5 receptor groups: α1 x2, α2 x3, β1 x2, β2 x5, β3 x1) under the three column heads RECEPTOR / TISSUE / EFFECT(S) — no diagram, no margin note, no printed mnemonic. RASTER CENSUS: pdf 258 carries exactly 3 sep rasters, ALL belonging to the UPPER portion's bladder illustration (the PH14 wiring diagram — COPYRIGHTED tissue artwork, never reproduced, NOT part of this topic); the LOWER table is PURE TEXT — nothing reproduced, nothing redrawn from imagery; the table is carried VERBATIM as the note's table block and conveyed as ONE original KYP grid (the AdrenergicReceptorDistributionMap: the 12-tissue x 5-receptor matrix with the 13 verbatim effect cells, the three seesaw cards, the four-code strip, the reading-rule footer). SECTION EXTENT verified: the section ENDS on pdf 258 at the table's last row; pdf 259 opens the SEPARATE pending 'G-protein–linked second messengers' section — sourcePages = [258] only. KYP extensions flagged wherever they appear: the grid view, the empty-cell caveat, the pancreas/tone seesaws, the α2 triple-brake reading, the Heart-vs-Cardiac-muscle doubling note, the drug/clinical anchors (albuterol, epinephrine, dobutamine, phenylephrine, clonidine, mirabegron, the JG apparatus), and the classic 'one heart, two lungs' counting code (printed on the FACING page's G-protein table, book 237 — a separate pending topic; attributed). The same-page cross-link (the upper portion's β₃ detrusor plate vs this table's β3 Adipose row) is pinned as boundary evidence. No copyrighted photographs reproduced; nothing reproduced.
